description: Rules applied to every generated scenario to catch impossible, inconsistent, or out-of-range synthetic data before it enters the final dataset. Scenarios failing a rule are logged and rejected, not silently dropped.

rules.rule: Salinity in [20, 41] psu; temperature in [-2, 32] deg C; no negative concentrations anywhere
final_total_alkalinity - initial_total_alkalinity = alkalinity_added exactly (mass balance of treatment)
DIC = CO2* + HCO3- + CO3(2-) reproduced within numerical tolerance
Total alkalinity recomputed from full speciation matches the input total alkalinity within tolerance
Baseline pH in [7.6, 8.4]; baseline aragonite saturation state in [0.5, 6]; baseline DIC in [1700, 2400] umol/kg, checked against published surface-ocean ranges (GLODAPv2 / Jiang et al. 2019)
Increasing dose must increase pH (state 1), decrease pCO2 (state 1), increase aragonite saturation state (state 1), and increase potential CO2 uptake, in every environment
Uptake efficiency (eta) strictly between 0 and 1 for every row with dose > 0 (cannot absorb more CO2 mol-for-mol than alkalinity added at these conditions)
Equilibrated-state pH must fall between baseline pH and immediate-state pH; dose = 0 rows show identically zero change in every derived quantity
Saturation state is monotonically consistent with carbonate ion concentration at fixed temperature and salinity
PyCO2SYS and the independent cross-check solver agree to within |delta pH| < 0.001 on a 500-row audit sample
Solver reproduces the published reference check values in Dickson, Sabine & Christian (2007)
Every column's unit is derived and explicitly stated in the data dictionary; a full units audit is performed before export
Statistical outlier scan (|z| > 4) on all calculated columns; each flagged row is either manually explained or its environment draw is rejected and logged
A rejected-scenario log is retained and reported in the methodology so nothing is silently dropped from the dataset
